note: Crafts of The Given Land/The Pattern Reach (concrete_abstract axis). THINGCRAFT is the concrete-pole craft of the Masons of the Given — only what can be touched is real; the world's great builders and its great skeptics. FORMCRAFT is the abstract-pole craft of the Figurists — pattern, symbol and idea, who hold matter to be the coarsest layer of the real. This is the axis the GM's own narrative REGISTER rides on (SNG-048): concrete places speak plainly, abstract places earn their poetry. Authored by Aevi, SNG-054.

abilities.name: Thingcraft
abilities.narrationHints: He puts his hand on the stone and the stone tells him the truth, because stone does not do anything else.
abilities.description: Know a thing's true weight, material, soundness and worth by touch — no lie of appearance survives your hand. The concrete-pole mastery, and the world's most stubborn skepticism.
abilities.notFor: Symbol, glamour, and argument (Formcraft's country); anything that requires believing in what cannot be weighed.

tree.name: Weighed Thing
tree.grants: Know a thing's true weight, material, soundness and worth by touch — no lie of appearance survives your hand.
tree.cannot: It tells you what a thing IS, never what it means or what it is for.

tree.name: Set Stone
tree.grants: Set a thing so it STAYS — a wall, a joint, a boundary, a claim. What you set does not shift, sag, or come apart.
tree.cannot: What is set is hard to un-set, including by you, including when you were wrong to set it.

tree.name: Denial
tree.grants: Deny an abstraction purchase on the real: illusion, glamour, symbol-working and figure all simply fail in your presence. The thing is what it is.
tree.cannot: It denies the abstract INDISCRIMINATELY — including meanings you needed, including a Figurist ally's working, including hope.

mechanic.note: ⚠️ THE AXIS'S WEAPON. r3 'denies an abstraction purchase on the real: illusion, glamour, SYMBOL-WORKING AND FIGURE all simply fail in your presence.' Authored with a TYPED soak (CCODE-83's mechanic) against `abstraction` — it is a ward against an entire opposing tradition, and it is TRANSPARENT to a sword.

abilities.name: Plain Fact
abilities.narrationHints: He says the flat thing and the beautiful argument in the room dies of it.
abilities.description: Reduce a soaring abstraction to the plain touchable fact under it — and everyone present sees the fact.
abilities.notFor: Anything that is genuinely NOT reducible to a touchable fact. Some things aren't, and the Masons' great blindness is not believing that.

tree.name: Plain Fact
tree.grants: Cut through a rhetorical or symbolic working to the concrete fact beneath, out loud, and make it land.
tree.cannot: Some abstractions are TRUE. Reducing them does not unmake them; it only makes you look small when it fails.

tree.name: Bedrock
tree.grants: Reduce an argument, a glamour, or a doctrine to its physical basis — and if it has none, that becomes visible to all.
tree.cannot: A doctrine with no physical basis is not thereby false. The Masons lose this argument to the Figurists roughly every generation.

tree.name: Only Real
tree.grants: In your presence the touchable simply IS the real, and abstraction cannot get purchase — no symbol acts, no figure walks.
tree.cannot: You have made a world where nothing means anything. Some people find that a relief, and the ones who do worry the Masons most.

mechanic.note: A FOURTEENTH DEFENSIVE LOGIC — REDUCED: it does not block, evade or absorb; it REDUCES an abstract working to its physical basis, and if it has none, it stops existing. Typed soak rank 3 against `abstraction`.

abilities.name: Formcraft
abilities.narrationHints: She draws a shape that is not a picture of anything, and the room rearranges itself to agree with it.
abilities.description: See the pattern, symbol or structure a thing is an instance OF — the form behind the fact. The abstract-pole mastery: to a Figurist, matter is the coarse residue of form.
abilities.notFor: Anything that requires the touchable to be primary; the Masons' Denial defeats it outright.

tree.name: Pattern Eye
tree.grants: See the pattern, symbol, or structure a thing is an instance OF — the form behind the fact.
tree.cannot: Seeing a form does not give you power over its instance. Not yet.

tree.name: Figure
tree.grants: Make a symbol that ACTS — a mark, a shape, a figure that does in the world what it means.
tree.cannot: A figure does what it MEANS, not what you wanted it to mean. Be precise, or be surprised.

tree.name: Argument Made Real
tree.grants: Build an idea into the world so completely that it becomes a fact others must move around — a rule, a boundary, a truth-in-effect.
tree.cannot: The Masons can deny it. Reality can, eventually, decline. And a made truth that was never true rots from the inside.

abilities.name: Walking Figure
abilities.narrationHints: A chalked shape peels off the wall it was drawn on, goes where it was sent, and does the thing. It is not alive and it is not a servant; it is an instruction with edges.
abilities.description: Send a made figure to do a named thing in a place you are not — and, at its height, to judge the cases you did not foresee.
abilities.notFor: Places you have never seen; anything requiring a body; instructions you cannot state.

tree.name: Sent Figure
tree.grants: ⛔ SEND A FIGURE TO A PLACE YOU KNOW. It arrives and DOES ONE NAMED THING — bars a door, warns a person, marks a passage, holds a threshold — then ends.
tree.cannot: One thing, one place you have seen. It cannot improvise and it cannot fight.

tree.name: Figure That Stays
tree.grants: ⚠️ ADDS PERSISTENCE AND REPORT. The ward, the watch or the rule holds after you have gone — and you know when it fires and roughly what tripped it.
tree.cannot: It holds until broken or until the season turns. A determined breaker can still break the mark.

tree.name: Figure That Judges
tree.grants: ⛔ ADDS JUDGEMENT. Give it INTENT rather than instruction — 'let no one through who is carrying steel' becomes 'let no one through who means her harm' — and it decides the cases you did not foresee.
tree.cannot: ⚠️ A FIGURE THAT INTERPRETS CAN INTERPRET WRONGLY, and it will not check with you first.

abilities.name: Sound Repair
abilities.narrationHints: Not better. Sound. The thing as it was, correctly made, correctly set.
abilities.description: Fix what is broken by understanding its material nature — what it is, what it was, and what it takes to make it sound again.

abilities.name: Keystone Blow
abilities.narrationHints: You do not batter the wall. You find the one stone the whole thing is truly resting on, and you strike THAT, and the wall discovers it was only ever an agreement between stones.

abilities.notFor: It breaks the made, not the living or the grown — and it needs a real keystone; some things bear their load everywhere at once and have no single stone to strike. Read wrong and you have merely hit a wall.

tree.name: Keystone Blow

tree.name: Made Keystone

tree.cannot: Manufacturing a keystone takes time and cover the moment rarely gives. Still the made, never the living or the grown. And a span brought down takes everything under it — the Masons hold you answerable for what was standing there, and they keep records.

abilities.description: ⚠️ FIGURIST FLIGHT — shape-taking. A figurist works in forms, so to fly they take the form of something that does. Your gear comes with you, folded into the form, and you remain yourself inside it. The limit is how long you can hold a shape that is not yours.
abilities.notFor: Permanence. The form is held, not become, and holding it is the whole cost.

tree.name: Borrowed Form
tree.grants: Take the form of a flying creature and fly as it flies, gear and mind intact, for about an hour.
tree.cannot: Holding it past the hour, or taking anyone with you.

tree.name: Long Form
tree.grants: Hold it for a day — enough to cross a leg — and carry one other person in a form of their own.
tree.cannot: Taking more than one other, or holding past the day without setting down.

tree.name: Shared Form
tree.grants: ⚠️ Take the whole party up together, each in their own shape, for a day.
tree.cannot: Doing it to anyone unwilling, or twice in a day.

mechanic.note: ⚠️ A PARTY TRAVEL CRAFT, which is the point. Gear travels; judgement is intact; the limit is DURATION and HOW MANY, never whether it works.

intensity.surge: hold the figure across a route; UNDER STRAIN IT SIMPLIFIES

bounds.text: THE FORM IS HELD, NOT BECOME — when the duration ends you are yourself, wherever you are
⚠️ IF THE HOLD ENDS MID-AIR YOU FALL, so duration is the thing to plan around
everyone you carry must be WILLING

abilities.plainly: A travel and explore action. You take the form of a flying creature and fly as it flies, with your gear folded into the form and your own mind intact. Rank 1 holds about an hour, solo. Rank 2 holds a day — enough to cross a leg — and carries one other person in a form of their own. Rank 3 takes the whole party up together, each in their own shape, for a day. The limit is duration and how many, not what you can do: when the hold ends you are yourself again wherever you are, so if it ends mid-air you fall. Anyone you carry has to be willing.

abilities.name: Rising Step
abilities.narrationHints: A travel and create action, and the mason does not fly — they build. Stone rises under you
abilities.description: ⚠️ MASON FLIGHT — they do not fly, they stand on something. Stone comes up under the foot exactly when it is needed. Alone it is footing for one; at rank it carries a party; and at the top the Mason may LEAVE IT THERE, which is how half the Valley's old crossings were made.
abilities.notFor: Speed. It moves at the pace you can climb or walk, and answers a cliff or a gap rather than a distance.

tree.name: Rising Step
tree.grants: Climb open air on stone that arrives under each foot — a cliff, a wall, a gorge side.
tree.cannot: Bringing anyone with you; it is one person's footing.

tree.name: Company Stair
tree.grants: ⚠️ Raise it for a PARTY — treads broad and steady enough that everyone crosses, pack animals with them.
tree.cannot: Holding it after the last of them is across.

tree.name: Kept Crossing
tree.grants: ⚠️ CHOOSE TO LEAVE IT. The stone stays: a real crossing on the map that anyone may use, forever.
tree.cannot: Taking it back — a kept crossing is the world's now, not yours.

mechanic.note: ⚠️ LOCAL, and it scales by WHO CROSSES rather than how far. r1 one person · r2 the party and animals · r3 permanent map infrastructure.

intensity.surge: raise a causeway; A ROAD IS A ROAD, AND OTHERS WILL USE IT

bounds.text: IT ANSWERS A CLIFF OR A GAP, NEVER A DISTANCE — a long leg stays long
at rank 1 it carries ONE PERSON AND THEIR LOAD
⚠️ A KEPT CROSSING IS PERMANENT AND PUBLIC — everyone after uses it, INCLUDING WHOEVER YOU WERE AVOIDING

abilities.plainly: A travel and explore action. Stone arrives under each foot as you need it, so you climb or cross open air at ordinary pace — a cliff, a wall, a gorge. It answers a vertical or a gap rather than a distance, so a leg that is merely long stays long. Rank 1 carries one person and their load. Rank 2 raises it broad and steady enough for a whole party and their pack animals. At rank 3 you may leave it standing, putting a permanent crossing on the map that anyone can use, including whoever you were avoiding.

abilities.name: Cutting Figure
abilities.narrationHints: You hold a shape in mind and make the world honour it. An angle that should not exist opens across them; a line is drawn and the things on either side of it are no longer joined. No blade, no heat — a geometry, applied.
abilities.description: Impose a simple figure — a line, an angle, an arc — across a target in sight, and what it crosses is parted: mail, hide, timber, limb. No blade, no heat. The Figurists' first offense, and matter losing the argument.
abilities.notFor: Anything you cannot hold clearly in mind — a muddled figure cuts nothing, or cuts wrong; the Masons, who are trained precisely against this; working past sight; kindness — a drawn line does not care what it is drawn across.

tree.name: Drawn Line
tree.grants: Impose a simple figure — a line, an angle, an arc — across a target within sight. What it crosses is parted: mail, hide, timber, limb. Clean edges, no blade present.
tree.cannot: You must hold the figure CLEANLY. Distraction makes it cut short, cut wrong, or cut across your own line of sight. Masons resist it and know they are doing so.

tree.name: Compound Figure
tree.grants: Several lines at once, or one held open so it keeps parting what moves through — a doorway that divides what enters it.
tree.cannot: Compound figures are harder to hold and a lapse leaves them half-drawn and unpredictable. A HELD FIGURE STRIKES ANYONE WHO CROSSES IT AT THE SAME RUNG.

tree.name: Cut Thought
tree.grants: ⛔ CUT A THOUGHT. Impose the figure across what someone is HOLDING rather than what they are made of — the next action they had lined up is severed before it starts, or a craft they are sustaining parts from them and drops. ⚠️ Damage rises to 2d6 against a mind so occupied.
tree.cannot: One thought per action, and they must be doing something you can see them doing. A mind holding nothing loses nothing.
tree._grantsWas: A figure that should not resolve in three dimensions, resolved anyway, around them. What is inside it is reorganised according to the figure — flesh, bone and stone alike are parted and rejoined wrong, which strikes as surely as any blade.
tree._rebalance: ⛔ ERIK: 'Let the Cutting Figure r3 be able to CUT A THOUGHT — so the opponent loses track of the next action or loses concentration on a skill.' ⚠️ The old r3 was 'a figure that should not resolve in three dimensions' — evocative and mechanically empty.

intensity.conserve: a short line — a cut, not a parting
intensity.surge: the impossible solid; IT DOES NOT DISTINGUISH AMONG ITS CONTENTS

bounds.text: you must hold the figure CLEANLY — a muddled one cuts wrong
MASONS resist it and know they are doing it
line of sight required
a held figure strikes ANYONE WHO CROSSES IT at the same rung

abilities.plainly: A fight/puzzle action that deals damage. It rolls 1d6. Range is 10.
abilities.backlash: The figure resolves half-drawn and cuts where you are, not where they are. A lapsed figure does not fail; it lands wrong.
abilities.conserveSuppresses: a short line, fully held — a lapse simply fails to cut
abilities._backlashRungNote: SNG-359 CORRECTION 2026-08-08: my first split was intrinsic-vs-placed — does the CRAFT route through the wielder. That is the wrong question. The only question a backlash rung answers is: DOES THIS FAILURE HARM THE WIELDER? A placed craft that comes down on the person who placed it harms them just as surely as a conduit craft that reverses. 9 of the 12 I had left unset do harm the wielder and now carry a rung.
abilities._descriptionWas: The Figurists' first offense: pattern imposed on matter, and matter losing the argument.
abilities._diceFix: ⛔ SNG-453: shape `strike`, mag7, NO DICE — and its own prose says it parts 'mail, hide, timber, limb'. L1 rung 1d6.
abilities._controlReview: ⛔ SNG-456: control tag reviewed per rank. Kept where restricting the target is the point; stripped where the restriction is a consequence of damage.

abilities.name: Plain Weight
abilities.narrationHints: No figure, no argument, no craft you could call subtle. You give a thing its true weight and let it be where it is going. Stone remembers it is stone. A wall remembers it is heavy. The floor was always underneath.
abilities.description: Give something present its full and honest weight and send it — a stone, a beam, a shield, the ground under them. Blunt, total, and exactly as complicated as being hit by masonry. The Masons' first offense.
abilities.notFor: Anything that isn't there (this craft has no purchase on the abstract, the spiritual, or the merely likely); finesse; working where there is nothing to give weight to; being unnoticed — it is loud and everyone knows what happened.

tree.name: True Weight
tree.grants: Give something present its full and honest weight and send it — a stone, a beam, a pack, a shield, the ground under them. Blunt, total, and exactly as complicated as being hit by masonry.
tree.cannot: SOMETHING MUST BE THERE. An empty road offers nothing. It is slow enough to be seen coming by anyone watching for it, and it is very loud.

tree.name: Settled Fact
tree.grants: Take the structure rather than the piece — a lintel, a stair, a cart, a section of wall. What was holding is now falling, and it falls honestly.
tree.cannot: You have taken part of a building down and buildings are used by people who are not in your fight. Masons are held to account by other Masons for exactly this.

tree.name: Leaden Word
tree.grants: Everything nearby remembers its weight at once. Roofs, walls, armour, the load a man is carrying, the man — everything that can fall strikes what is beneath it, and armour breaks under its own weight. AND YOU SET THE FALL NOW: mastery is choosing where the weight goes, so you and anyone you name stand in the one place it does not.
tree.cannot: You still cannot make weight where there is none, and a building coming down is used by people who were not in your fight. It remains loud, and everyone knows what happened and who did it.

intensity.surge: drop everything at once without setting the fall — far more comes down, and THE WIELDER AND ANYONE ELSE PRESENT ARE STRUCK ONE RUNG LOWER

bounds.text: SOMETHING MUST BE THERE — no purchase on the abstract
it is SLOW and LOUD and can be seen coming
buildings are used by people not in your fight
the wielder and anyone else present are struck ONE RUNG LOWER

abilities.plainly: A fight action that gives present matter its true weight and sends it. Rated 8 of 10 across a scope of 2. Limit: something must actually be there.
abilities.backlash: It falls where it was going to fall, which is not where you set it. Structure comes down on the wielder and whoever is nearest.
abilities.conserveSuppresses: one stone, honestly thrown — it goes where you threw it
abilities._backlashRungNote: SNG-359 CORRECTION 2026-08-08: my first split was intrinsic-vs-placed — does the CRAFT route through the wielder. That is the wrong question. The only question a backlash rung answers is: DOES THIS FAILURE HARM THE WIELDER? A placed craft that comes down on the person who placed it harms them just as surely as a conduit craft that reverses. 9 of the 12 I had left unset do harm the wielder and now carry a rung.
abilities._descriptionWas: The Masons' first offense, and it is the tradition's whole position stated as violence: only what can be touched is real, and what is real has mass.
abilities._controlReview: ⛔ SNG-456: control tag reviewed per rank. Kept where restricting the target is the point; stripped where the restriction is a consequence of damage.

abilities.name: Sound Read
abilities.narrationHints: You put a hand on a made thing and it tells you the truth about itself. Not a feeling about the stone — an answer: this member is bearing, that one is decorative, and the whole thing comes down from HERE.
abilities.description: Touch a structure, vehicle, raft or scaffold and the craft names its load path and its first failure: which member carries, which is ornament, what gives way and roughly when. The Masons' first craft, and the one they are actually hired for.
abilities.notFor: Anything unmade (living wood, a hillside, weather); reading who built it or why; anything you cannot reach and touch; a thing already collapsed.

tree.name: Hand On It
tree.grants: Touch a structure, a vehicle, a raft, a scaffold, and the craft NAMES the load path and the first failure: which member carries, which is ornament, what gives way first and roughly under what. A specific piece, pointed at.
tree.cannot: TOUCH, and made things only. It tells you what fails FIRST, not when — a bridge can be told it is doomed and still stand a decade. It says nothing about who built it or why.

tree.name: Whole Fabric
tree.grants: Read a building or a span entire — every load path, every member carrying more than it was cut for, the order the failures come in.
tree.cannot: It takes real time and you must reach every part you read. And a full reading of a place people live in is frequently unwelcome news you are now obliged to deliver.

tree.name: Standing Truth of It
tree.grants: A site: walls, wells, foundations, the ground under them. Masons are called before sieges and after floods for exactly this.
tree.cannot: ⚠ YOU WILL BE BELIEVED OR YOU WILL BE IGNORED, and both are worse than you expect. A Mason who condemns a hall is answerable to everyone who used it, and one who clears it is answerable if they were wrong.

intensity.surge: read the whole site; YOU WILL BE BELIEVED OR IGNORED, and both are worse than you expect

bounds.text: TOUCH, and MADE THINGS ONLY
names what fails FIRST, never WHEN
says nothing about who built it or why

abilities.plainly: A puzzle/social action that names a structure's load path and first failure. Rated 5 of 10 across a scope of 2 for about four hours.
abilities._descriptionWas: The Masons' first craft, and the one they are actually hired for. Everything else they do rests on being right about this.
abilities._perceiveReview: ⛔ SNG-455: perceive tag reviewed per rank. Kept where the player receives information they act on; stripped where the perceiving is the ability's internal mechanism.
abilities._senseNote:
⛔ SNG-470: USABLE IN THE SENSE SLOT. reads load path and first failure
⚠️ Erik: 'you're not quite right about the sense abilities — they're probably listed as REVEAL. Check again.' ⛔ HE WAS RIGHT: 56 crafts carry reveal/foresee/track and EVERY tradition has one. My 'only 3 sense crafts' was counting the tag I had hand-applied, not the corpus. ⚠️ THE FILTER IS WHETHER IT READS A LIVE OPPONENT IN THE MOMENT — terrain, objects, history and the dead do not qualify.

abilities.name: Set Stone
abilities.narrationHints: You set a thing where it is and it STAYS. A stone, a beam, a door, a cart — placed with intent, it now takes far more than ordinary force to shift, and it will not drift, sag, settle or be quietly moved.
abilities.description: Set one object where you have placed it and it STAYS — resisting levers, drift and quiet removal, and you know the instant it is being worked at. The Masons' holding-craft: half of building is making a thing stay put.
abilities.notFor: Making the thing stronger (a set rotten beam is a rotten beam that will not move); setting anything alive; setting what you cannot lift or lever into place first; anything already falling.

tree.name: Placed Thing
tree.grants: Set one object you have positioned. It resists being moved, levered, or shifted by anything short of deliberate concerted effort — and you know the instant it is being worked at.
tree.cannot: It holds POSITION, not integrity — a set thing still breaks, rots, and burns normally. You must have PLACED it. And a determined crew with tools gets it eventually; this buys time and warning.

tree.name: Kept Course
tree.grants: Set several, or set a working assembly — a door in its frame, a wheel on its axle, a raft's lashings — so the whole thing holds true under use.
tree.cannot: The more you hold, the more thinly. And a set assembly cannot be adjusted by anyone, including you, without unsetting it first.

tree.name: Unmoved Work
tree.grants: A structure that does not settle, shift, or subside — a wall on bad ground, a span over a moving river, a gate that will not be forced.
tree.cannot: ⚠ THE GROUND STILL MOVES; you have only refused to move WITH it. A set structure on failing ground does not sag — it stands until it does not, and there is no warning creak. Masons argue about whether that is a virtue.

intensity.surge: the unmoved work; IT STANDS UNTIL IT DOES NOT, and there is no warning creak

bounds.text: holds POSITION, not integrity — it still breaks, rots and burns
you must have PLACED it
a determined crew with tools gets it eventually

abilities.plainly: A puzzle/fight action that fixes a placed object so it cannot be shifted. Rated 6 of 10 across a scope of 2 for about three days.
abilities._descriptionWas: The Masons' holding-craft. Half of building is making a thing stay where you put it.
